assays.assay_description: Mice with a head-mounted neodymium magnet were placed in a 12.5-cm diameter glass cylinder surrounded by a magnetometer coil; head twitches were counted over 20–40 min sessions. Includes dose-response testing of 25N/25O/2C2 derivatives and classical psychedelics, antagonist/pretreatment blockade of DOI-induced HTR (25N-N1-Nap, 25N-NBPh, 25N-NB-2-OH-3-Me, pimavanserin), ICV YM-254890 and systemic edelfosine signalling-inhibitor experiments, and a repeated-dosing tolerance (tachyphylaxis) challenge.

application_type.evidence: 25N derivatives ... were injected SC (5 mL/kg or 10 mL/kg); pimavanserin, edelfosine, R-(-)-DOI, (±)-DOI ... were injected IP (5 mL/kg); YM-254,890 was injected into the lateral ventricle (2 µL) over 1 min.

setup_habituation.evidence: HTR experiments were conducted in a well-lit room, and the mice were allowed to habituate to the room for at least 1 h prior to testing (room habituation only; no apparatus habituation described).

setup_restrain.evidence: Mice were tested in a 12.5-cm diameter glass cylinder surrounded by a magnetometer coil; no restraint described.

food_restriction.evidence: food and water provided ad libitum except during behavioral testing

water_restriction.evidence: food and water provided ad libitum except during behavioral testing

time_to_assay.evidence: Mice were pretreated with vehicle or drug, (±)-DOI (1 mg/kg IP) was injected 10 minutes later, and then HTR activity was assessed for 20 minutes; in tolerance experiments mice were challenged 24 hours after the last of five daily injections.

sample_size.evidence: In the first experiment, mice (n = 6-7/group, 19 total) were injected SC ... In the second experiment, mice (n = 6/group, 12 total) ...

outcomes.summary: HTR magnitude was used as a behavioural proxy for psychedelic potential. Balanced/high Gq-efficacy agonists (e.g., 25N-NBOMe, 25O-NBOMe, 2C2-NBOMe, 25O-NBcP, LSD, psilocin, 5-MeO-DMT, DET) induced robust head twitches, whereas β-arrestin-biased or low-Gq-efficacy compounds (25N-N1-Nap, 25N-NBPh, 25N-NB-2-OH-3-Me, 25D-N1-Nap, 25O-NB-3-I, 25O-NBPh-10'-OH, lisuride, 2-Br-LSD, 6-F-DET, 6-MeO-DMT) did not; the biased agonists instead blocked DOI-induced HTR, as did ICV YM-254890 (Gq/11 inhibitor) and the PLC inhibitor edelfosine. Repeated 5-day dosing with 25N-N1-Nap or DOI (but not pimavanserin) produced tolerance to a DOI challenge 24 h later.
outcomes.evidence: 25N-NBOMe (4) induces the head-twitch response (HTR) (W 5,19.46 = 84.56, p < 0.0001). 25N-N1-Nap (16) does not induce the HTR (F 5,26 = 1.39, p = 0.2618). Pretreatment with 25N-N1-Nap (16) blocks the HTR induced by (±)-DOI (F 3,16 = 68.43, p < 0.0001).

B1_num_measures.evidence: HTR counts from individual male C57BL/6J mice as well as group means are shown — head twitch count is the only reported behavioural measure.

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: HTR counts were analyzed using one-way ANOVAs or one-way Welch ANOVAs — total counts per session, no within-session time bins reported.

B3_sequential_structure.evidence: No analysis of behavioural transitions, sequences or bout microstructure reported.

B4_ethological.evidence: The head-twitch response is a 5-HT2AR-mediated involuntary head movement; per rubric HTR is not an ethological behaviour.

B5_social.evidence: Mice were tested individually in a glass cylinder; no social construct.

B6_cognitive.evidence: No learning, memory or cognitive-flexibility component.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Head twitches were identified in the recordings off-line by their waveform characteristics or using artificial intelligence — i.e., a supervised machine-learning classifier labelling a discrete behavioural event.

B8_multivariate.evidence: Only univariate ANOVAs and bivariate correlations were used; no PCA/clustering of behavioural features.

assays.assay_name: Locomotor Activity in the Behavioral Pattern Monitor (PCP-induced hyperactivity)
assays.assay_description: Mice were placed in a 30 × 60 cm transparent Plexiglas BPM chamber with infrared photobeam position detection; distance traveled was recorded for 60 minutes and analysed in 20-minute blocks, after SC pretreatment with 25N-N1-Nap or M100907 and IP PCP (5 mg/kg) or vehicle.

application_type.evidence: mice (n = 6/group) were pretreated SC with test drug or vehicle, PCP (5 mg/kg) or vehicle was injected IP 10 minutes later.

setup_habituation.evidence: Mice were allowed to habituate to the testing room for at least 1 h prior to testing (room habituation only; no prior exposure to the BPM chamber described).

setup_restrain.evidence: The position of the mouse in x,y coordinates is recorded by a grid of 12 × 24 infrared photobeams — the animal moves freely in the chamber.

food_restriction.evidence: food and water provided ad libitum except during behavioral testing

water_restriction.evidence: food and water provided ad libitum except during behavioral testing

time_to_assay.evidence: mice were pretreated SC with test drug or vehicle, PCP (5 mg/kg) or vehicle was injected IP 10 minutes later, and then the mice were placed in the BPM chambers 10 minutes after the second injection.

sample_size.evidence: N = 6 male C57BL/6J mice/group (four pretreatment × treatment groups per experiment).

outcomes.summary: The β-arrestin-biased 5-HT2A agonist 25N-N1-Nap attenuated PCP-induced hyperlocomotion (distance traveled) at a dose that did not alter baseline activity, mirroring the effect of the 5-HT2A-selective antagonist M100907.
outcomes.statistics: 25N-N1-Nap: pretreatment × PCP F(1,20)=7.09, p=0.015; pretreatment × PCP × time F(2,40)=11.03, p=0.0002. M100907: pretreatment × PCP F(1,20)=7.41, p=0.0131. Tukey post hoc, α=0.05.
outcomes.evidence: 25N-N1-Nap (16) attenuates phencyclidine (PCP)-induced hyperactivity (pretreatment × PCP: F 1,20 = 7.09, p = 0.015; pretreatment × PCP × time: F 2,40 = 11.03, p = 0.0002).

B1_num_measures.evidence: Locomotor activity was quantified as distance traveled, which was analyzed in 20-minute blocks — only distance traveled is reported as a result.

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Locomotor activity was quantified as distance traveled, which was analyzed in 20-minute blocks ... with time as a within-subject variable.

B3_sequential_structure.evidence: No analysis of behavioural sequences or transitions reported.

B4_ethological.evidence: Although the BPM can detect rearing and holepoking, only distance traveled is reported for these experiments.

B5_social.evidence: Each mouse was tested alone in its own BPM chamber; no social component.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: The position of the mouse in x,y coordinates is recorded by a grid of 12 × 24 infrared photobeams — a beam-break position tracking system.

B8_multivariate.evidence: Three-way ANOVA on a single measure; no dimensionality reduction or multivariate behavioural analysis.

E1_environment_type.evidence: Each mouse BPM chamber is a transparent Plexiglas box with an opaque 30 × 60 cm floor, enclosed in a ventilated isolation box.

E2_shelter.evidence: No shelter or refuge is described in the BPM chamber.

E3_bedding.evidence: Opaque 30 × 60 cm floor; no bedding described.

E4_nesting.evidence: No nesting material described in the chamber.

E5_enrichment.evidence: Only wall and floor holes equipped with photobeams for holepoking detection; no enrichment objects described.

E6_spatial.evidence: A single rectangular 30 × 60 cm chamber without internal partitions.

E7_social_context.evidence: Each mouse BPM chamber ... the mice were placed in the BPM chambers — tested individually.

E8_food_water.evidence: food and water provided ad libitum except during behavioral testing

D1_continuity.evidence: the mice were placed in the BPM chambers 10 minutes after the second injection and activity was recorded for 60 minutes.

D3_recording_days.evidence: A single BPM test session per animal is described.

D4_baseline.evidence: No pre-drug baseline locomotor recording reported; mice were placed in the chamber after injections.

D5_followup.evidence: Recording began 20 minutes after drug administration; no recording ≥24 h post-dose.

D6_circadian.evidence: Session duration was 60 minutes, less than 6 hours.

judge_notes: Only two behavioural paradigms are present: the head-twitch response (magnetometer) and locomotor activity in the behavioral pattern monitor. All BRET, calcium flux, NanoBiT internalization, docking and MD work was excluded as non-behavioural.

All HTR variants (dose-response of ~17 25N/25O/2C2 derivatives, classical psychedelics vs non-psychedelics, DOI-blockade pretreatment experiments, ICV YM-254890, systemic edelfosine, and the 5-day repeated-dosing tolerance challenge) were merged into ONE HTR assay per the rubric's assay-identity rules.
B1 for HTR set to 0 (head-twitch count is the sole reported measure), overriding deepseek's speculative '2-3'.

B7 for HTR scored 1 following deepseek: 'Head twitches were identified ... using artificial intelligence' is a supervised ML behavioural classifier, not simple position tracking (confidence medium because detection is from magnetometer waveforms rather than video).
B1/B4 for the BPM assay scored 0: although the apparatus can detect rearing and holepoking, the paper explicitly reports only distance traveled for these experiments (overrides qwen).

D1/D3 for HTR scored as multiple sessions/2-7 days based on the explicit statement 'Mice were tested in multiple HTR experiments, with at least 7 days between studies', plus the 5-day dosing + day-6 challenge design; D5 scored Yes for the 24-h post-regimen tolerance challenge.

setup_habituation set to not_reported for both assays — the paper reports only testing-room acclimation (1 h), which the rubric explicitly excludes from apparatus habituation (overrides deepseek's 'yes').
Gemma4 output was schema-broken (no B/E/D item scores) and contributed only to metadata consensus.
DOI reported in the dosing list because it is a psychedelic 5-HT2A agonist administered as both a test compound and a challenge agent; vehicle-only controls omitted.
